Connect this series arrangement to Hooke's law $F = kx$, rearranged as $x = F/k$, with $F = 80 \text{ N}$ and $k$ in $\text{N cm}^{-1}$ to give $x$ directly in $\text{cm}$.

walkthrough: Identify the arrangement from the diagram: the springs are in series, one below the other, so each spring carries the full $80 \text{ N}$ load.
State the governing rule: for each spring obeying Hooke's law, $F = kx$, so extension $x = F/k$.
For the upper spring, $x_1 = 80/6.0$ with $F$ in $\text{N}$ and $k$ in $\text{N cm}^{-1}$, giving $x_1 \approx 13.3 \text{ cm}$.
For the lower spring, $x_2 = 80/4.0$, giving $x_2 = 20 \text{ cm}$.
In series the total extension adds: $x = x_1 + x_2 \approx 13.3 + 20 = 33.3 \text{ cm}$, which is about $33 \text{ cm}$ with units of length as expected.
